result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Calculate edge current-flow betweenness counting only flow from sources to targets. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Calculate edge current-flow betweenness counting only flow from sources to targets. title: >- [Graph.edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Calculate edge current-flow betweenness counting only flow from sources to targets. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate edge current-flow betweenness counting only flow from sources to targets. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L47558-L47659){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset( sources, targets, normalized=True, weighted=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge current-flow betweenness on a subset](/assets/graphs/edge-current-flow-betweenness-centrality-subset.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with the sources A and B and the target G outlined; only current sent from A or B to G counts. Edges are drawn thicker the more of it they carry: all of it crosses E-F and F-G, which share the top at 0.033, while inside the triangles the current spreads out, C-E 0.018 down to C-D 0.003." width="100%"} Each node in `sources=` sends a unit of current to each node in `targets=`, and an edge scores the total current it carries. Current spreads over all routes in proportion to their conductance, so this shows which links a flow between two sets of nodes actually uses: the lines feeding a set of cities from a set of plants, or the ties a message crosses between two groups. Edge weights act as conductances; self-loops score `0`. The graph must be undirected and connected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Nodes that inject current, as integer IDs or string labels. [targets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Nodes that extract current, as integer IDs or string labels. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), divide by `2 (n - 1)(n - 2)`; otherwise by `4`. Both match NetworkX's `edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset()`, and with every node as a source and a target they reproduce `edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality()`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights as conductances. If `None` (default), follows the graph. Weights must be positive. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the edge attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as an edge attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping edge IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected, a node does not exist, or a weight is not positive. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The current on an edge for a unit flow from `s` to `t` is its conductance times the potential difference across it, read from the inverse of the grounded Laplacian. The sum runs over ordered source-target pairs, $O(|S| |T|)$ per edge. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a ring of six nodes, current from `A` to `D` splits evenly between the two halves, so every edge carries the same share. Sent to the neighbor `B` instead, most of the current takes the direct edge `A-B`: ::: {#1295c7ea .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ring = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEF")) ring.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "A")]) label = ring.get_label_from_id def carried(target): scores = ring.edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset( ["A"], [target], normalized=False, return_dict=True ) return { "-".join(label(n) for n in ring.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(e)): round(s, 3) for e, s in scores.items() } carried("D"), carried("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ({'C-D': 0.125, 'A-B': 0.125, 'E-F': 0.125, 'F-A': 0.125, 'D-E': 0.125, 'B-C': 0.125}, {'C-D': 0.042, 'A-B': 0.208, 'E-F': 0.042, 'F-A': 0.042, 'D-E': 0.042, 'B-C': 0.042}) ``` ::: :::
